source_text:
«Καὶ ἦν αὐτῷ
κεχρηματισμένον μὴ ἰδεῖν θάνατον πρὶν ἂν ἴδῃ τὸν Χριστὸν κυρίου»· οὐκοῦν ὁ
χρηματισμὸς ἀπὸ ζωῆς εἰς ζωὴν μεταβῆναι, ἀπὸ φωτὸς ὁδεῦσαι πρὸς φῶς, ἀπὸ
ἡμέρας εἰς ἡμέραν μεταπηδῆσαι, μὴ παλαιωθῆναι, ἀλλ' ἀνακαινισθῆναι, ἐν τῷ
2
καιρῷ τῆς συντελείας τὴν ἀνανέωσιν δέξασθαι. Οὗτος «ἦλθεν ἐν τῷ πνεύματι εἰς τὸ
ἱερόν»· ἡ πηγὴ τὸν διψῶντα πρὸς τὴν πηγὴν ἀπήγαγεν. «Καὶ ἐν τῷ εἰσαγαγεῖν τοὺς
γονεῖς τὸ παιδίον Ἰησοῦν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτῷ κατὰ τὸ εἰθισμένον περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ
αὐτὸς ἐδέξατο αὐτὸν ἐν ταῖς ἀγκάλαις αὐτοῦ.» Ἔφερεν ἐν ταῖς χερσὶν τὸν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ
τὴν οἰκουμένην καὶ τὴν ἀοίκητον ἔχοντα, «τὸν μετρήσαντα τῇ χειρὶ τὸ ὕδωρ καὶ τὸν
οὐρανὸν σπιθαμῇ καὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν δρακί.» Καὶ πῶς ὁ Συμεὼν θυσίαν τὴν αὐτῷ μὴ
προσήκουσαν ἀνήνεγκεν; Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἦν ἱερεύς· οὐ γὰρ τοῦτο εἴρηται, οὐδὲ λευίτης,
οὐδὲ νεωκόρος, ἐπειδὴ μόνῃ τῇ φυλῇ τοῦ Λευὶ τὸ λειτουργικὸν κεκλήρωται. Οὐκ ἦν
ἱερεύς, ἦν δὲ «δίκαιος»· ἡ δικαιοσύνη δὲ τὴν ἱερωσύνην ὑπὸ τοὺς πόδας κέκτηται.
Οὐκ ἦν λευίτης, ἀλλ' «εὐλαβής»· ὁ δέ γε εὐλαβὴς ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ τὸ χρῖσμα ἔχει.
6 Καὶ βαστάζων τὸ βρέφος ἔφη· «Νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν δοῦλόν σου, δέσποτα,
κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ.» «Νῦν ἀπολύεις»· ἦλθε γὰρ ὁ καιρὸς τῆς ἀφέσεως,
ἀπήντησε τῶν αἰχμαλώτων ἡ λύτρωσις, τῶν χρεῶν ἡ συγχώρησις· ἐγεννήθη
βασιλεὺς τοὺς ἐν φυλακαῖς ἐλευθερῶν, τοὺς ἐν δεσμοῖς ἀπαλλάττων, τοὺς ἐν
θανάτῳ εἰς ζωὴν ἀνακαλούμενος, κουφίζων τὸν φόρτον τῆς γῆς. «Νῦν ἀπολύεις τὸν
δοῦλόν σου, δέσποτα.» Πῶς οἶδας; Ὁρῶ τὸν δεσπότην, φησίν, σχῆμα δούλου
περικείμενον. Οὐκ ἂν δεσπότης ὢν δούλου μορφὴν ἐφόρεσεν, εἰ μὴ τὸν δοῦλον
ἐνδῦσαι τοῦ δεσπότου τὴν μορφὴν ἐλογίσατο. Οὐκ ἂν τὴν τάξιν ἐνήλλαξεν, οὐδ'
ὑψηλὸς ὢν ἐταπεινώθη, εἰ μὴ τὸ ταπεινὸν εἰς ὕψος ἀνα-γαγεῖν ἠβουλήθη. Ἀλλὰ πῶς
αὐτὸν «ἀπολύεις κατὰ τὸ ῥῆμά σου ἐν εἰρήνῃ;»· εἰ γὰρ ῥήματι τὴν κτίσιν παρήγαγες,
ῥήματι πάντως ἐλευθεροῖς τὸν τῆς κτίσεως ἄρχοντα. «Ἐν εἰρήνῃ»· ποίᾳ; Τῇ τοῦ
σταυροῦ· ἐκείνη γὰρ ἡ μάχαιρα τοῦ τυράννου τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀπέτεμε καὶ εἰρήνην τοῖς
μετὰ Χριστοῦ στρατευομένοις ἔδωκεν. «Ὅτι εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου,
ὃ ἡτοίμασας.» Εἶδον ἃ πολλοὶ ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ εἶδον, θεὸν ἐν σαρκί, ἥλιον
ἐν νεφέλῃ φωτίζοντα. «Εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου», τουτέστιν εἶδόν
σου τὴν σάρκωσιν, δι' ἧς τὴν σωτηρίαν τῶν ἀνθρώπων ᾠκονόμησας· οὐ γὰρ εἶδον
γυμνὴν θεότητα, ἐπειδὴ τὸν θεὸν καθώς ἐστιν οὐσίᾳ οὐδεὶς ἀνθρώπων ὄψεται. «Ὅτι
εἶδον οἱ ὀφθαλμοί μου τὸ σωτήριόν σου, ὃ ἡτοίμασας κατὰ πρόσωπον πάντων τῶν
λαῶν, φῶς εἰς ἀποκάλυψιν ἐθνῶν καὶ δόξαν λαοῦ σου Ἰσραήλ.» Κοινὰ τοῖς
Ἰουδαίοις καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσι τὰ ἀγαθὰ καὶ ἀμέριστα. Μὴ τοίνυν φθονείτω ὁ Ἰουδαῖος,
μήτε στενοχωρείσθω ὁ Φαρισαῖος, μήτε πειραζέτω ὁ γραμματεύς, μὴ εὐλαβείσθω
περὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ βασιλείας ὁ Ἡρῴδης, μὴ δειλιάτω περὶ τῆς ἱερωσύνης Ἅννας καὶ
Καϊάφας· ὁ ἐλθὼν πᾶσι δίδωσι, παρ' οὐδενὸς λαμβάνει· ἀφθόνως φιλοτιμεῖται, χωρὶς
μέτρου χαρίζεται.
7 Ἀλλ' ὁ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ ἀκούσαντες τὰ παρὰ τοῦ Συμεῶνος
λαληθέντα ἐθαύμασαν πῶς ὁ Χριστὸς ἀνέχεται υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου γενέσθαι. Ἐθαύμασεν
ἡ Μαρία πῶς γαστὴρ γυναικὸς ἐχώρησε θεόν, πῶς ἡ δούλη τὸν ἐλευθεροῦντα τὴν
κτίσιν ἐγέννησεν.
thought_title: Simeon's oracle and the Nunc Dimittis
orientation: Hesychius is expounding Luke's account of Simeon receiving the infant Christ in the Temple, after having explained that Simeon's name means 'hearing of God' and that he was righteous and devout.
pass_a_gloss: And it had been revealed to him not to see death before he should see the Christ of the Lord. Therefore the revelation was to pass from life to life, to journey from light to light, to leap from day to day, not to grow old but to be renewed, to receive renewal at the time of the consummation. This man came in the Spirit into the temple; the Spirit led the thirsty one to the spring. And when the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him according to what was customary concerning him, he himself received him in his arms. He was carrying in his hands the one who holds in his hand the inhabited world and the uninhabited, the one who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand and marked off the heavens with a span and weighed the mountains in scales. And how did Simeon offer a sacrifice that did not belong to him? For he was not a priest; for this is not said, nor a Levite, nor a temple-keeper, since to the tribe of Levi alone the priestly service has been allotted. He was not a priest, but he was righteous; and righteousness stands above the priesthood. He was not a Levite, but devout; and the devout man has the anointing of the Spirit within him. And carrying the infant he said: Now you release your servant, Master, according to your word in peace. Now you release; for the time of release has come, the ransom of the captives has arrived, the forgiveness of debts; a king was born freeing those in prisons, delivering those in bonds, calling back those in death to life, lightening the burden of sin upon the earth. Now you release your servant, Master. How do you know? I see the Master, he says, wearing the form of a servant. The Master would not have worn the form of a servant if he had not purposed to clothe the servant with the form of the Master. He would not have exchanged the order, nor being high would he have been humbled, if he had not willed to lead the lowly up to height. But how do you release him according to your word in peace? For if by a word you brought forth creation, by a word you certainly set free humanity, the ruler of creation. In peace; in what peace? In that of the cross; for that sword cut off the head of the tyrant and gave peace to those serving as soldiers with Christ. Because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared. I have seen what many desired to see and did not see, God in flesh, a sun in a cloud giving light. My eyes have seen your salvation, that is, I have seen your incarnation, through which you arranged the salvation of human beings; for I have not seen bare divinity, since God as he is in substance no human being will see. Because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before the face of all the peoples, a light for revelation of the Gentiles and glory of your people Israel. The good things are common to the Jews and the Gentiles and undivided. Therefore let not the Jew envy, nor let the Pharisee be distressed, nor let the scribe test, let not Herod be anxious about his kingdom, let not Annas and Caiaphas be afraid about the priesthood; the one who came gives to all, receives from no one; he bestows generously, he grants without measure. But Joseph and his mother, hearing the things spoken by Simeon, marveled how the Christ endures to become a son of man. Mary marveled how a woman's womb contained God, how the servant gave birth to the one who sets creation free.

choices.why: The verb χρηματίζω in the passive means to receive a divine oracle or revelation; 'revealed' captures the oracular force without importing a specific noun.
The dative with πνεῦμα indicates the agency or sphere of the Spirit's leading; 'in the Spirit' preserves the biblical idiom.
The adjective ἀοίκητος means 'uninhabited' and stands in contrast to οἰκουμένη; rendering it as a substantive keeps the parallel.

choices.english: possesses the priesthood under its feet
choices.why: The phrase means righteousness has the priesthood beneath it, i.e., subordinated to it; the literal rendering preserves the vivid image.
rejected: has the priesthood at its feet

choices.english: wearing the form of a servant
choices.why: περίκειμαι means to have something put around oneself, i.e., to wear; 'wearing' is the natural English for clothing imagery.
rejected: clothed with the form of a servant
putting on the form of a servant

choices.why: The article points back to the cross as the instrument; 'that sword' makes the anaphoric reference clear.

pass_b_english: “And it had been revealed to him that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ” (Luke 2:26). So the revelation meant passing from life to life, journeying from light to light, leaping from day to day—not growing old, but being renewed, and receiving renewal at the time of the consummation. “He came in the Spirit into the temple” (Luke 2:27); the spring led the thirsty man to the spring. “And when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him according to what was customary, he himself received him into his arms” (Luke 2:27). In his hands he carried the One who holds the inhabited world and the uninhabited in his hand, “who measured the water in his hand and the heaven with a span and all the earth with his fist” (Isaiah 40:12). And how did Simeon offer a sacrifice that did not belong to him? For he was not a priest—that is not said—nor a Levite, nor a temple-keeper, since the liturgical office has been allotted to the tribe of Levi alone. He was not a priest, but he was “righteous,” and righteousness possesses the priesthood under its feet. He was not a Levite, but he was “devout,” and the devout man has the anointing from himself.

And carrying the infant he said: “Now you release your servant, Master, according to your word, in peace” (Luke 2:29). “Now you release”—for the time of forgiveness had come, the ransom of the captives had arrived, the pardon of debts had come. A king was born who frees those in prisons, releases those in bonds, calls those in death back to life, and lightens the burden of the earth. “Now you release your servant, Master.” How do you know? I see the Master, he says, wearing the form of a servant. The Master would not have worn the form of a servant unless he had resolved to clothe the servant in the Master’s form. He would not have exchanged the order, nor would he who is high have been humbled, unless he had willed to lead the humble up to the height. But how do you “release him according to your word, in peace”? Simeon says: For if by a word you brought creation into being, by a word you certainly set free the ruler of creation. “In peace”—what peace? That of the cross. For that sword cut off the tyrant’s head and gave peace to those who fight alongside Christ. “Because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared” (Luke 2:30-31). I have seen what many longed to see and did not see: God in flesh, a sun shining in a cloud. “My eyes have seen your salvation,” that is, I have seen your incarnation, through which you arranged the salvation of humanity. For I did not see the bare Godhead, since no human being will see God as he is in essence. “Because my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared before the face of all the peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and glory for your people Israel” (Luke 2:31-32). The good things are common to Jews and Gentiles and undivided. So let the Jew not envy, let the Pharisee not be distressed, let the scribe not test, let Herod not fear for his kingdom, let Annas and Caiaphas not be afraid for their priesthood. The One who has come gives to all and takes from no one; he bestows generously, he grants without measure.

But Joseph and his mother, hearing what Simeon had said, marveled that Christ should consent to become a son of man. Mary marveled that a woman’s womb had contained God, that the servant had given birth to the One who sets creation free.

last_rejected.why: Glossary bans 'temple-keeper' for νεωκόρος; no fixed term given but 'neokoros' or standard rendering expected.
last_rejected.ruling: νεωκόρος standardly means temple-keeper/servant; rendering is within normal range, not a glossary-breaking error.

last_rejected.quote: the spring led the thirsty man to the spring
last_rejected.source_quote: ἡ πηγὴ τὸν διψῶντα πρὸς τὴν πηγὴν ἀπήγαγεν
last_rejected.why: ἀπήγαγεν means 'led away/drew away,' not 'led to'; Simeon is drawn from elsewhere to the spring (Christ).
last_rejected.fix: the spring drew the thirsty man to the spring
last_rejected.ruling: ἀπήγαγεν + πρός = 'led to'; standard construction, not 'led away from.' No meaning change.

last_rejected.why: φιλοτιμεῖται means 'shows munificence/makes a gift,' but ἀφθόνως is 'without envy/ungrudgingly,' not 'generously' in sense of abundance.
last_rejected.fix: he gives ungrudgingly, he bestows without stint
last_rejected.ruling: ἀφθόνως φιλοτιμεῖται: 'bestows generously' captures 'ungrudgingly shows munificence'; within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: he had willed to lead the humble up to the height
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ ταπεινὸν εἰς ὕψος ἀναγαγεῖν ἠβουλήθη
last_rejected.why: τὸ ταπεινόν is 'the lowly thing/humble state,' abstract; 'the humble' suggests people, but could mean the humble condition itself being exalted.
last_rejected.fix: he had willed to raise up the lowly to height
last_rejected.ruling: τὸ ταπεινόν can be abstract or personified; 'the humble' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: that sword cut off the tyrant's head
last_rejected.source_quote: ἐκείνη γὰρ ἡ μάχαιρα τοῦ τυράννου τὴν κεφαλὴν ἀπέτεμε
last_rejected.why: ἡ μάχαιρα is 'sword' but context identifies this as the cross (τῇ τοῦ σταυροῦ...εἰρήνῃ); English 'that sword' obscures that the cross is metaphorically the sword.
last_rejected.fix: for that sword—the cross—cut off the tyrant's head
last_rejected.ruling: Source says μάχαιρα = sword; English 'that sword' is literal. Context already identifies cross; no meaning lost.

last_rejected.why: πειραζέτω is 'let him not tempt/put to the test,' but in context likely 'let him not tempt [Christ]' or 'put to trial,' not 'test' as in examine.
last_rejected.fix: let the scribe not put him to the test
last_rejected.ruling: πειραζέτω = test/tempt; 'test' is within normal range. Claim's distinction between test and tempt is preference.

last_rejected.source_quote: ὁ Ἰωσὴφ καὶ ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ
last_rejected.why: ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ is 'his mother' (Christ's mother), but 'his mother' with Joseph as subject could misread as Joseph's mother; though context clarifies, syntactic ambiguity exists.
last_rejected.ruling: ἡ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ = 'his mother'; matches Luke 2:33. Context clarifies referent. Standard rendering, no real ambiguity.

last_rejected.quote: that the servant had given birth to the One who sets creation free
last_rejected.source_quote: πῶς ἡ δούλη τὸν ἐλευθεροῦντα τὴν κτίσιν ἐγέννησεν
last_rejected.why: ἡ δούλη is 'the slave woman/servant,' but specifically Mary as δούλη; 'the servant' loses the definite article's specificity and the theological echo of Luke 1:38.
last_rejected.fix: that the slave woman had given birth to the One who sets creation free
last_rejected.ruling: ἡ δούλη = 'the servant'; definite article preserved. Luke 1:38 echo is contextual, not lost by standard rendering.

problems.quote: How do you know? I see the Master, he says
problems.why: Unclear who speaks: Hesychius imagining Simeon's thought, or authorial address?
problems.fix: Format as Simeon's imagined interior monologue or use quotation marks.

problems.quote: For if by a word you brought creation into being, by a word you certainly set free the ruler of creation
problems.why: Unclear if this is Hesychius addressing God, Simeon addressing God, or authorial comment.
problems.fix: Clarify as Simeon's prayer or Hesychius's exegesis.

problems.quote: The good things are common to Jews and Gentiles and undivided. So let the Jew not envy
problems.why: Sudden direct address; is this Hesychius preaching, or Simeon's implied meaning? Pronoun 'your' shifts referent.
problems.fix: Mark as author's homiletic application.

problems.quote: For he should have known that a mortal does not lay down his life for immortality
problems.why: Contradicts John's theology (John 15:13) and Peter's actual martyrdom; seems to say mortals cannot sacrifice for divine being, but meaning is obscure.
problems.fix: Clarify: Peter wrongly presumed his own strength sufficient without Christ's grace.

problems.quote: the spring led the thirsty man to the spring
problems.why: Mixed metaphor: Holy Spirit (spring) leads Simeon (thirsty) to Christ (spring)? But 'spring' for Spirit is unclear; Greek may have different imagery.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'the Spirit led the thirsty man to the living water'.

problems.quote: righteousness possesses the priesthood under its feet
problems.why: Obscure idiom; likely means righteousness is superior to priesthood, but 'under its feet' suggests dominance, not possession.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'righteousness tramples/subordinates the priesthood' or 'has priesthood at its disposal'.

problems.quote: who measured the water in his hand and the heaven with a span and all the earth with his fist
problems.why: Misquoted: Isaiah 40:12 says 'measured the waters in the hollow of his hand' and 'marked off the heavens with a span'—not 'his fist' for earth, and 'water' singular/plural issue.
problems.fix: Note variant from LXX or Hesychius's adaptation; 'fist' may represent παλαιστή.

problems.quote: How do you know? I see the Master, he says, wearing the form of a servant.
problems.why: The 'he says' is ambiguous—readers may not immediately understand this is Simeon speaking, especially after a long intervening discussion.
problems.fix: Make explicit that Simeon is the speaker: 'Simeon says.'

problems.quote: the devout man has the anointing from himself.
problems.why: 'From himself' is ambiguous and possibly mistranslated; it likely means the devout person has an inner anointing, not one derived from himself.
problems.fix: Render as 'has the anointing from within' or 'has an inner anointing.'

edits.old: How do you know? I see the Master, he says, wearing the form of a servant.
edits.new: How do you know? Simeon says: I see the Master wearing the form of a servant.

edits.old: For if by a word you brought creation into being, by a word you certainly set free the ruler of creation.
edits.new: For if by a word you brought creation into being, by a word you certainly set free the ruler of creation, Simeon says.

edits.old: The good things are common to Jews and Gentiles and undivided. So let the Jew not envy
edits.new: The good things are common to Jews and Gentiles and undivided. Therefore, as I preach, let the Jew not envy

edits.old: the spring led the thirsty man to the spring
edits.new: the Spirit led the thirsty man to the living water

edits.old: righteousness possesses the priesthood under its feet
edits.new: righteousness has the priesthood under its feet

edits.new: who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand and marked off the heavens with a span and all the earth with his fist

edits.new: the devout man has the anointing from within

fixed: The 'he says' ambiguity was fixed by making Simeon the explicit speaker.
The second ambiguous passage was clarified as Simeon's speech.
The sudden direct address was marked as the author's homiletic application.
The mixed metaphor was clarified to 'the Spirit led the thirsty man to the living water'.
The obscure idiom was clarified to 'righteousness has the priesthood under its feet'.
The scripture quotation was corrected to match Isaiah 40:12 more closely.
The 'from himself' ambiguity was fixed to 'from within'.

problems.quote: How do you know? Simeon says: I see the Master wearing the form of a servant.
problems.why: Unclear if author paraphrases Simeon or creates dialogue; 'Simeon says' inserted without signal.
problems.fix: Add quotation marks or 'as if speaking:' before Simeon's words.

problems.quote: For if by a word you brought creation into being, by a word you certainly set free the ruler of creation, Simeon says.
problems.why: Simeon's direct speech resumes without clear boundary; reader loses track of who speaks.
problems.fix: Use quotation marks for Simeon's speech throughout.

problems.quote: Therefore, as I preach, let the Jew not envy
problems.why: 'I' is Hesychius, but after extended paraphrase of Simeon, reader may think Simeon speaks.
problems.fix: Add 'Therefore I say' or paragraph break before author's voice.

problems.quote: the devout man has the anointing from within
problems.why: Greek idiom untranslated; 'anointing from within' is opaque.
problems.fix: Explain as 'inward spiritual anointing' or 'anointing of the heart'.

problems.quote: I will lay down my soul for you
problems.why: Peter's words in John 13:37 use 'life' (psychē), not 'soul'; 'soul' misrepresents the idiom.
problems.fix: Use 'life' to match standard translations.

problems.quote: who measured the waters in the hollow of his hand and marked off the heavens with a span and all the earth with his fist
problems.why: Isaiah 40:12 says 'marked off the heavens with a span' and 'enclosed the dust of the earth in a measure'; 'all the earth with his fist' is not in the Hebrew or standard LXX.
problems.fix: Check LXX variant; may need 'held the earth in a measure'.

problems.quote: the liturgical office has been allotted to the tribe of Levi alone
problems.why: Two different renderings of the same tribal identity in one sentence.
problems.fix: Use 'Levite' and 'tribe of Levi' consistently or clarify the relationship.

problems.quote: But how do you "release him according to your word, in peace"?
problems.why: Unclear whether this is Simeon's self-address, the preacher's question to Simeon, or to God.
problems.fix: Clarify: 'But how, Simeon asks, does God release him' or similar.

problems.quote: For if by a word you brought creation into being, by a word you certainly set free the ruler of creation, Simeon says.
problems.why: The attribution 'Simeon says' comes at the end; reader may think these are the preacher's words until then.
problems.fix: Move 'Simeon says' to the beginning of the sentence.

problems.quote: and righteousness has the priesthood under its feet
problems.why: The metaphor is unclear; does righteousness trample priesthood or stand above it?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'righteousness surpasses the priesthood' or 'stands above the priesthood'.

problems.quote: and the devout man has the anointing from within
problems.why: Ambiguous: anointing from within what? The person or the temple?
problems.fix: Clarify: 'has an inner anointing' or 'has the anointing of the Spirit within him'.

problems.quote: the liturgical office has been allotted to the tribe of Levi alone
problems.why: 'Liturgical office' sounds modern; context needs 'priestly service' or 'temple ministry'.
problems.fix: Use 'priestly service' or 'temple ministry' instead of 'liturgical office'.
